newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Unemployment moves won't hit budget - Sweden FinMin.
newsitem.headline: Unemployment moves won't hit budget - Sweden FinMin.

text.p: Sweden's Finance Minister Erik Asbrink said on Tuesday that measures to fight unemployment will not disrupt budget targets.
"There will be room for the economic-political measures that will be taken to fight unemployment within the budget-political targets," Asbrink told the Swedish parliament during a debate.
But he also said unemployment was the key issue and that the minority Social Democratic government aims to keep its promise to halve the number of jobless to the year 2000 to around four percent.
"We are regaining freedom of action and measures will be presented in the spring budget proposal (on April 15)," he said.
He emphasised that it was only possible to fight unemployment with sound state finances.
In February, Swedish unemployment stood at 8.8 percent, according to Statistics Sweden.
